title: Contrapuntal notes — Ashby Kline (runtime infra)
body:
Quick take:
- Strong systems intuition; thinks in trade-offs rather than single silver bullets.
- Comfortable with low-level memory/latency discussions but less confident on infra product tradeoffs (quota/tenant isolation).
- Paired well on a small async batching problem — clear about invariants but missed an edge-case in KV eviction under preemption.

Signals (positive):
- Explained KV-cache/kv-index interplay using a concrete example (prefix-heavy prompts); proposed a cheap heuristic to keep hot-prefix entries pinned for short bursts.
- Good mental model for batching: prioritized latency SLOs, suggested adaptive batch size using P50/P95 window rather than static cap.
- Debugging style: small hypotheses, quick experiments, ties observations back to measurable metrics.

Noise / weaker signals:
- High-level cloud tenancy experience is mostly on single-tenant dedicated clusters; limited exposure to multi-tenant quota enforcement at scale.
- ML/ops product tradeoffs (billing granularity, legal/compliance concerns) not explored; likely needs partner with product/Sales for enterprise discussions.

Deep-dive probes we ran and notes:
1) KV-cache eviction under preemption scenario (whiteboard + pseudo-code)
   - Ashby sketched LRU + frequency hybrid and then proposed a preemption callback to checkpoint hot keys.
   - Missed a race where checkpointing could temporarily inflate memory usage causing cascading OOMs.
   - Follow-up: explicitly ask about backpressure strategies (drop, pause, spill-to-disk).

2) Adaptive batching micro-coding (pairing exercise)
   - Implemented controller: target_latency = configured_slo - safety_margin; adjust batch size up/down based on recent latency samples.
   - Edge-case: slow tail requests (cold KV) cause oscillation; Ashby suggested smoothing but hadn't implemented hysteresis.

3) Observability / alerting thought experiment
   - Proposed useful metrics: token-level p50/p95 latency, batch-size distribution, cache-hit rate by prefix, eviction rate, preemption/GC events per host.
   - Good orientation toward actionable alerts (e.g., rising eviction rate + rising P95).

Assessment on practical checklist (binary-ish):
- Pair-programming: competent, good trade-off calls (pass)
- Whiteboard architecture: clearly communicates, draws failure modes (pass)
- Tenancy & billing product nuance: needs mentoring (weak)
- Oncall temperament: calm, asks clarifying questions, good logs-first approach (pass)

Onboarding / probation ramp idea (30/60/90 sketch):
- 30d: shipping a small improvement — complete the adaptive batching controller spike, add integration test that simulates variable tail latencies.
- 60d: own a medium story — implement safer checkpointing for KV hot keys; add a spill-to-disk fallback and a metric to track spill frequency.
- 90d: reliability/ops deliverable — lead a small rollout on dedicated capacity, run canary with failure injection and validate SLA targets.

Open questions before hire decision:
- Has Ashby worked with HSM/KMS or strict audit environments before? (legal/compliance exposure).
- How do they design for multi-tenant metering? Any prior experience with token-level billing or quota enforcement?
- What are concrete examples of production incidents they led? Need timeline and impact.

Recommendation / gut call:
- Lean hire for senior runtime engineer (strong SRE + systems tilt).
- Hire with the expectation of pairing them with an eng/product lead for enterprise-facing tenancy/billing nuances for first 2 quarters.
- Offer hinge: 6-month check-in focused on ownership of a tenancy/billing adjacent project.

Quick action items (for interview packet):
- Ask follow-up: describe a production incident where checkpointing/spill-to-disk was used or should have been used.
- Assign a short take-home: design a simple quota enforcement mechanism that tolerates transient preemption and produces billable metrics (2-3 hours).

Notes to self (meta):
- Candidate shows pattern: prefers pragmatic prototypes + measurable outcomes. Good fit for small team pushing reliability-first features.
- Watch for over-reliance on single-host heuristics; probe distributed corner-cases more deeply if moving forward.

End of scratchpad.
